arxiv-1406-7317.title: Combinatorial Interpretation of General Eulerian Numbers Thanks: Michigan State University Thanks: Novato, CA
arxiv-1406-7317.creator: Tingyao Xiong
arxiv-1406-7317.description: Abstract Since 1950s, mathematicians have successfully interpreted the traditional Eulerian numbers and q − q- Eulerian numbers combinatorially. In this paper, the authors give a combinatorial interpretation to the general Eulerian numbers defined on general arithmetic progressions { a , a + d , a + 2 ​ d , … } \{a,a+d,a+2d,\dots\} .

arxiv-1811-10771.title: Event-Based Structured Light for Depth Reconstruction using Frequency Tagged Light Patterns
arxiv-1811-10771.creator: T. Leroux, S.-H. Ieng, R. Benosman University of Pittburgh, Carnegie Mellon Univeristy, Sorbonne Universitas
arxiv-1811-10771.description: Abstract This paper presents a new method for 3D depth estimation using the output of an asynchronous time driven image sensor. In association with a high speed Digital Light Processing projection system, our method achieves real-time reconstruction of 3D points cloud, up to several hundreds of hertz.

arxiv-2204-04599.title: Optimal Round and Sample-Size Complexity for Partitioning in Parallel Sorting Conference: Proceedings of the 35th ACM Symposium on Parallelism in Algorithms and Architectures; June 17–19, 2023; Orlando, FL, USA Proceedings of the 35th ACM Symposium on Parallelism in Algorithms and Architectures (SPA
arxiv-2204-04599.creator: Wentao Yang, Vipul Harsh, Edgar Solomonik
arxiv-2204-04599.description: Abstract . State-of-the-art parallel sorting algorithms for distributed-memory architectures are based on computing a balanced partitioning via sampling and histogramming. By finding samples that partition the sorted keys into evenly-sized chunks, these algorithms minimize the number of communication rounds required. Histogramming (computing positions of samples) guides sampling, enabling a decrease in the overall number of samples collected.

arxiv-2303-00636.title: Classifying the age of a glass based on structural properties: A machine learning approach
arxiv-2303-00636.creator: Giulia Janzen, Casper Smit ∗, Samantha Visbeek, Vincent E. Debets, Chengjie Luo, Cornelis Storm, Simone Ciarella, Liesbeth M.C. Janssen
arxiv-2303-00636.description: Abstract It is well established that physical aging of amorphous solids is governed by a marked change in dynamical properties as the material becomes older. Conversely, structural properties such as the radial distribution function exhibit only a very weak age dependence, usually deemed negligible with respect to the numerical noise.

arxiv-2406-16714.title: AutoDetect : Towards a Unified Framework for Automated Weakness Detection in Large Language Models
arxiv-2406-16714.creator: Jiale Cheng, Yida Lu, Xiaotao Gu, Pei Ke, Xiao Liu, Yuxiao Dong , Hongning Wang , Jie Tang , Minlie Huang
arxiv-2406-16714.description: Abstract Although Large Language Models (LLMs) are becoming increasingly powerful, they still exhibit significant but subtle weaknesses, such as mistakes in instruction-following or coding tasks. As these unexpected errors could lead to severe consequences in practical deployments, it is crucial to investigate the limitations within LLMs systematically.

arxiv-2409-00853.title: JaxLife: An Open-Ended Agentic Simulator
arxiv-2409-00853.creator: Chris Lu, Michael Beukman, Michael MatthewsJakob Foerster FLAIR, University of Oxford, United Kingdom
arxiv-2409-00853.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chris Lu, Michael Beukman, Michael MatthewsJakob Foerster FLAIR, University of Oxford, United Kingdom. Human intelligence emerged through the process of natural selection and evolution on Earth. We investigate what it would take to re-create this process in silico . While past work has often focused on low-level processes (such as simulating physics or chemistry), we instead take a more targeted approach, aiming to evolve agents that can accumulate open-ended culture and technologies across generations.

arxiv-2409-14874.title: Towards Ground-truth-free Evaluation of Any Segmentation in Medical Images Thanks: Work in progress. A. Senbi and T. Huang contributed equally.
arxiv-2409-14874.creator: Ahjol Senbi, Tianyu Huang, Fei Lyu, Qing Li, Yuhui Tao, Wei Shao, Qiang Chen, Chengyan Wang, Shuo Wang, Tao Zhou, Yizhe Zhang
arxiv-2409-14874.description: Abstract We explore the feasibility and potential of building a ground-truth-free evaluation model to assess the quality of segmentations generated by the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and its variants in medical imaging. This evaluation model estimates segmentation quality scores by analyzing the coherence and consistency between the input images and their corresponding segmentation predictions.

arxiv-2503-21697.title: The commutativity problem for effective varieties of formal series, and applications Thanks: Partially supported by the ERC grant INFSYS, agreement no. 950398, and the Polish National Science Centre grant no. 2024/54/E/ST6/00287.
arxiv-2503-21697.creator: Lorenzo Clemente
arxiv-2503-21697.description: Abstract A formal series in noncommuting variables Σ \Sigma over the rationals is a mapping Σ ∗ → Q \Sigma^{*}\to\mathbb Q from the free monoid generated by Σ \Sigma to the rationals. We say that a series is commutative if the value in the output does not depend on the order of the symbols in the input.

arxiv-2504-13794.creator: Mark Moeller, Tiago Ferreira, Thomas Lu, Nate Foster, Alexandra Silva
arxiv-2504-13794.description: Abstract . NetKAT is a domain-specific programming language and logic that has been successfully used to specify and verify the behavior of packet-switched networks. This paper develops techniques for automatically learning NetKAT models of unknown networks using active learning. Prior work has explored active learning for a wide range of automata (e.g., deterministic, register, Büchi, timed etc.

arxiv-2507-16606.title: Scalar-induced Neutrinoless Double Beta Decay in S ​ U ​ ( 5 ) SU(5)
arxiv-2507-16606.creator: P. S. Bhupal Dev, Srubabati Goswami, Debashis Pachhar, Saurabh K. Shukla
arxiv-2507-16606.description: Abstract We discuss the role of heavy scalar fields in mediating neutrinoless double beta decay ( 0 ​ ν ​ β ​ β ) (0\nu\beta\beta) within the S ​ U ​ ( 5 ) SU(5) Grand Unified Theory framework, extended suitably to include neutrino mass.

arxiv-2510-04821.title: Geometric Mechanics of Thin Periodic Surfaces
arxiv-2510-04821.creator: Wenqian Sun, Yanxin Feng, Christian D. Santangelo, D. Zeb Rocklin
arxiv-2510-04821.description: Abstract Thin surfaces are ubiquitous in nature, from leaves to cell membranes, and in technology, from paper to corrugated containers. Structural thinness imbues them with flexibility, the ability to easily bend under light loads, even as their much higher stretching stiffness can bear substantial stresses.

Multi-drug resistant (MDR) bacteria have become a major concern in hospitals worldwide and urgently require the development of new antibacterial molecules. Peptide deformylase is an intracellular target now well-recognized for the design of new antibiotics. The bacterial suscepti

plos-pone-0011762.title: FOXP3 Expression Is Upregulated in CD4 + T Cells in Progressive HIV-1 Infection and Is a Marker of Disease Severity
plos-pone-0011762.creator: Melinda S. Suchard, Elizabeth Mayne, Victoria A. Green et al.
plos-pone-0011762.description: PLOS ONE research article. Understanding the role of different classes of T cells during HIV infection is critical to determining which responses correlate with protective immunity. To date, it is unclear whether alterations in regulatory T cell (Treg) function are contributory to progression of HIV infect

pmc-11484875.title: RABIF promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression through regulation of mitophagy and glycolysis
pmc-11484875.creator: Ning Feng, Rui Zhang, Xin Wen, Wei Wang, Nie Zhang, Junnian Zheng, Longzhen Zhang, Nianli Liu
pmc-11484875.description: The RAB interacting factor (RABIF) is a putative guanine nucleotide exchange factor that also functions as a RAB-stabilizing holdase chaperone. It has been implicated in pathogenesis of several cancers. However, the functional role and molecular mechanism of RABIF in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are not entirely known.

pmc-11508498.title: Ultralow Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) Levels and Improved Oncological Outcomes in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer (mHSPC) Patients Treated with Apalutamide: A Real-World Multicentre Study
pmc-11508498.creator: Alicia López-Abad, Mario Belmonte, Miguel Ramírez Backhaus, Gerardo Server Gómez, Enrique Cao Avellaneda, Cristóbal Moreno Alarcón, Pedro López Cubillana, Pablo Yago Giménez, Pedro de Pablos Rodríguez, María José Juan Fita, Miguel Ángel Climent Durán, Iris Guardiola Ruiz, Natalia Vidal Crespo, Juan
pmc-11508498.description: Background/Objectives: Androgen receptor-targeted agents have significantly improved the prognosis of metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels are key prognostic markers, with rapid and deep reductions associated with better outcomes. This study aims to assess the association between the new PSA cut-offs and survival in mHSPC patients treated with Apalutamide.

pmc-12548116.title: Nitrogen–phosphorus stoichiometry shapes seedling growth and yield performance of perennial cool-season forage grasses in saline–alkali soil
pmc-12548116.creator: Nan Xu, Junpeng Niu, Zhipeng Guo, Quanzhen Wang, Zhao Chen
pmc-12548116.description: Grass production faces increasing challenges due to excessive fertilization, which contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and poor soil quality, especially in saline–alkali regions, threatening long-term sustainability. Most previous studies have focused on short-term effects of nitrogen (N) or phosphorus (P) applied individually, with limited understanding of their interactive and long-term impacts.

pmc-12577037.title: Exploring the quality of life of school-aged children with disabilities in Saudi Arabia and their educational inclusion: from caregiver’s perspectives
pmc-12577037.creator: Afnan Gmmash, Nourah Alamoudi, Shatha Alrehaili, Reem Basuodan, Mashael Alsobhi, Rawan Aldhabi, Abdullah Alqarni, Majed Albadi, Muataz Almaddah
pmc-12577037.description: BackgroundDisabilities limit the children’s ability to use their body freely, fully engage with their surroundings, participate in the community, and access services. These restrictions could adversely impact their academic progress in schools. This study’s primary aim is to report the quality of life of school-aged children and the percentage of children attending schools.

pmc-12591763.title: Quantitative metrics of mean apparent propagator magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis of axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer
pmc-12591763.creator: Xingke Huang, Jiayi Huang, Yingmei Tang, Wei Jiang, Qiongchao Jiang, Minxi Shen, Zehong Yang, Mengzhu Wang, Qin Li, Yeqing Liu, Xu Yan, Guang Yang, Ya Qiu, Xiang Zhang
pmc-12591763.description: BackgroundThe diagnosis of axillary lymph nodes (ALNs) status using only morphological criteria or conventional apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) value is not sufficiently accurate. Mean apparent propagator (MAP) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers the potential for discriminating metastatic and nonmetastatic ALNs.

pmc-12608885.title: Effects of Long-Term Nutrient Input on Progeny Seed Nutrient Contents, Germination and Early Growth Characteristics of Typical Coastal Wetland Plants
pmc-12608885.creator: Rong Hu, Sifan Peng, Bo Guan, Hongxiang Zhang, Fanzhu Qu, Xuehong Wang, Zhikang Wang, Jisong Yang, Feilong Huang, Guangmei Wang, Guangxuan Han
pmc-12608885.description: Seed reproduction is a vital stage in the life cycle of plants. In coastal wetlands, where nutrient regimes are increasingly altered by climate change and anthropogenic inputs, understanding how long-term nutrient enrichment affects progeny seed germination and early seedling establishment is essential for predicting vegetation shifts.

pmc-12642951.title: Recent advances in total synthesis of illisimonin A
pmc-12642951.creator: Juan Huang, Ming Yang
pmc-12642951.description: Illicium sesquiterpenes are a large class of highly oxygenated and sterically congested sesquiterpenoids isolated from the genus Illicium. Illisimonin A stands out as one of the most structurally intricate members of this family, featuring a novel bridged tricyclo[5.2.1.01,5]decane carbon framework designated as the “illisimonane” skeleton.

pmc-12688575.title: Serum electrolytes as prognostic markers: a new frontier in acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) management
pmc-12688575.creator: Shuting Chang, Mingming Chen, Yunpeng Xu, Donglun Li, Xue Han, Qiuyu Chen, Jian Liu
pmc-12688575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is the fourth leading cause of death worldwide, and acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) is the most common cause of hospitalization in these patients. This study demonstrated for the first time that serum sodium and calcium imbalances are independent predictors of AECOPD prognosis and explored the relationship between serum electrolyte levels and the prognosis of patients with AECOPD.MethodsThis retrospective study included 535 AECOPD patients admitted to The First Hospital of Lanzhou University between October 2021 and May

pmc-12866098.title: Comparative evaluation of the therapeutic efficacy between human amniotic epithelial cells and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells in premature ovarian insufficiency
pmc-12866098.creator: Qinyu Zhang, Jie Wang, Zixin Cheng, Wenjiao Cao, Qiuwan Zhang, Dongmei Lai
pmc-12866098.description: BackgroundPremature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a clinically challenging condition characterized by amenorrhea and infertility in women less than 40 years of age. Although both human amniotic epithelial cells (hAECs) and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSCs) have shown promise in treating POI, their comparative therapeutic efficacy and mechanisms remain poorly understood.

pmc-13060581.title: Faulting triggered by a quasi-diffusionless shear transition of olivine in deep subducted slabs
pmc-13060581.creator: Kohei Matsuda, Tomohiro Ohuchi, Sayako Inoué, Yuji Higo, Noriyoshi Tsujino, Sho Kakizawa, Takeshi Sakai
pmc-13060581.description: To clarify the process of faulting triggered by the olivine-ringwoodite transition in deep subducted slabs, we conducted deformation experiments on mantle olivine at pressures of 15 to 20 gigapascals and temperatures of 870 to 1320 kelvins. Throughgoing faulting occurred as a result of shear localization to “soft” gouge layers, which mainly consist of kinked olivine grains.

pmc-13334008.title: Flexible autonomic nervous system dynamics underlie attentional engagement in infancy
pmc-13334008.creator: Isabella C Stallworthy, Amritha Varshini Devarajan, Lorena Santamaria, Xinchen Fu, Xing Xi Tan, Daniel Fatori, Guilherme V Polanczyk, Victoria Leong
pmc-13334008.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The autonomic nervous system, relatively understudied compared to the central nervous system, is thought to play a key role in supporting attentional engagement, a cornerstone of cognitive control in early development. To address the non-trivial challenges that complex autonomic signals present to traditional modeling, we leverage recurrence quantification analysis (RQA), an established nonlinear approach for quantifying the temporal organization of heart-rate dynamics.

pmc-13340326.title: Schiff base-assisted catalytic fabrication of TiO2 nanoparticles for antibacterial applications against multidrug-resistant strains
pmc-13340326.creator: Farasat Bibi, Ahtaram Bibi, Naila Khalid, Nazia Sultan, Mubbashir Hussain, Sandal Wafa, Abdul Rehman, Niaz Muhammad
pmc-13340326.description: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria poses a significant global health challenge, necessitating the development of novel antimicrobial agents. In this study, titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticles were synthesized via a sol-gel method using Schiff base (azomethine) complexes as catalytic ligands.

pmc-13476058.title: Burden of Hereditary Angioedema in Adults: Impact of Disease and Patient Characteristics
pmc-13476058.creator: Maureen Watt, Inmaculada Martinez Saguer, Ryan Murphy, Marie De La Cruz, Ricardo Zwiener, Mauricio Sarrazola, Anete S. Grumach

pmc-13644880.title: The Relationship between Air Pollution Exposure, Genetic Liability for Schizophrenia, and Brain Outcomes in the ABCD Study
pmc-13644880.creator: Giulia Cattarinussi, Yingzhe Zhang, Fabio Sambataro, Divyangana Rakesh, Paola Dazzan
pmc-13644880.description: Background and HypothesisAir pollution exposure has been associated with altered neurodevelopment and increased risk of schizophrenia. Individuals at high genetic risk may be more vulnerable to these effects. Here, we examined how air pollution relates to brain structure and functional connectivity in adolescents, and we tested for the first time whether genetic risk for schizophrenia exacerbates these effects.
